note: Hex literal with L suffix too large for long reached createBigInteger with the suffix attached; fix strips it under a new ternary whose else-branch keeps the original str, so preserved.

setNullString built quotedNullString from a possibly null quoteCharacter ('null...null'); fix reuses setQuote's computation, whose ternary keeps quoteCharacter when non-null, so the missing null default is an omission.
formatSplitTime converted the split duration with toMillisInt, limiting it to the int range of milliseconds (about 24.8 days); fix calls toMillisLong, a one-call substitution.
The same interface field found through several implemented interfaces was reported as ambiguous; the existing Validate condition gained the clause || match.equals(test).

do-while called isMatch before testing the index bound, so a position already at the pattern's end read past the buffer; loop rewritten as a pre-tested while, a wrong control-flow construct as with Cli-28.
nextGraph and nextPrint passed 126 as the exclusive end, so '~' (126) could never be generated; end raised to 127 in both, one fault.

Unrolling the parent type dropped unmapped variables nested in wildcard bounds; fix replaces top-level identity pre-seeding with a preserveUnmapped mode; second fault: generic array components were never substituted (new GenericArrayType branch).

Out-of-range 'u' values broke lenient week-date parsing: setWeekDate throws even when lenient, and the strategy converted them as if in range; adds CalendarBuilder's folding and a range guard, original expressions kept under them.

Digit run overflowing int made Integer.parseInt throw NumberFormatException out of the ParsePosition-based parse; try/catch around the original call now signals failure, so the removed line is preserved.

Builders forced every declared field accessible in a bulk pre-pass, excluded and static ones included; fix makes each accessible only after filtering (wrong order); second fault: EqualsBuilder/HashCodeBuilder read inaccessible fields unchecked.

Threads blocked in acquire() were never woken when the semaphore shut down, so they hung; shutdown now calls notifyAll and waiters throw, a concurrency and lifecycle fault despite the addition-only fix.

Wildcard-to-wildcard check required every upper bound of the subject to be assignable to each target bound, where one suffices; inner loop rewritten from all-of to any-of, a wrong rule rather than a wrong token.
get(name) and isMapped(name) did not guard a null name before the header-map lookup; get gained a ternary, isMapped's existing condition gained name != null, so one fault, MISSING_CLAUSE by rule 1.

append(Object) had no cycle detection, so self-referencing arrays or objects recursed until StackOverflowError; adds the registry check used by reflectionAppend, addition-only like Gson-16's missing visited set.

isParsable's hand-written scanner disagreed with the JDK parsers it names (e.g. '.' accepted); rewrite delegates to them, but the javadoc reverses the documented exclusion of scientific notation, so possibly a feature.
lastIndexOf(String) delegated with start index size - 1 instead of size, an off-by-one wrong value at the search's starting edge (relevant to an empty-string match at size).

Null parameter-type arrays caused NullPointerException in method and constructor matching; fix normalises them with nullToEmpty at each entry, the removed lines being only a dropped final and uses renamed to the normalised copy.

removeCommonFrames kept comparing past the first differing frame, removing later frames that matched by position; adds a break there, the equality expression, now negated, and remove call kept verbatim, like Cli-17's missing break.
formatPeriod kept its working period fields in int, which can overflow when larger units are folded into smaller ones over long periods; the six fields widened to long, a wrong-type substitution.
A string ending on the separator yielded a trailing empty token even when empty tokens were not to be preserved; addition-only guard preserveAllTokens || beg < len around the final add.

Removing sub-hour fields with Calendar.set shifted results by an hour in a DST overlap; adds arithmetic removal for millisecond, second and minute, original set kept as default, like Lang-65's missing LANG-59 block.

Event counter could overflow and wrap negative, letting an overloaded interval close the breaker; adds saturation at Long.MAX_VALUE in a ternary whose else-branch keeps the original sum, so preserved.
DATE converter relied on SimpleDateFormat's default lenient parsing, silently rolling over out-of-range fields such as Feb 30; fix calls setLenient(false) on both formats, an API-use fault.

Comment lines were ended with println(), which also writes the trailing delimiter meant for records; calls replaced by a new separator-only helper, a wrong-call substitution since the call sites are modified.
shuffle(array, random) overloads dereferenced a null array or Random; the same null guard, now documented as a no-op, added to all nine overloads, addition-only and one fault.

start or end beyond chars.length went unchecked, failing later on the array access; two validation branches added to the existing else-if chain, addition-only, though the symptom is the wrong exception.
A very negative size made size - str.length() overflow into a huge pad count; the null check's condition gained || size <= str.length() in all four leftPad/rightPad overloads, one fault.

SimpleDateFormat.parse(String) ignores trailing text, so a valid date followed by garbage was accepted; fix parses with a ParsePosition and requires full consumption, replacing the exception-driven locale fallback, an API-use fault.

Only String and Character took the quoted-string path, so other CharSequence values such as StringBuilder fell through to generic object handling; instanceof String widened to CharSequence, a wrong-type substitution.

Rejection cap max(64, gap * 10) ignored that each draw spans 2^gapBits values, so valid ranges with few acceptable values could exhaust it and throw; cap rescaled to 64 << gapBits, a wrong-value substitution.

Parser could not read the +hh:mm offset FastDatePrinter emits for three or more Z letters; adds a width >= 3 branch with an extended-offset strategy, the RFC 822 pattern kept as the ternary's else-branch.
On overflow toMillisSince bound the result by the instant's sign, which is opposite to the duration's, returning the wrong extreme; fix binds on duration.isNegative(), a wrong-variable substitution.
